survey: A round wall clock seen from the front, tilted slightly so the left side of the rim looks thicker. The thick orange rim is round and closed all the way around, and it sits flat against the green striped wall with a soft shadow, so nothing floats. Inside the rim is a white dial with 12 navy hour markers, longer at 12, 3, 6 and 9, and rows of small minute dots between them. Three hands share one hub in the centre, capped by a red pin. The navy hour hand points just past 10 and the navy minute hand points to about 2, which gives 10:10. The hour hand is shorter and thicker than the minute hand, as it should be. The thin red second hand has a short tail past the hub and its tip reaches the 5 marker. All the hands stay inside the dial and could turn freely around the hub. Nothing is invented: no extra knobs, glows or parts a real clock wouldn't have.
